Evidence/CLM-039
Evidence record

A public interface is not the same thing as the underlying dataset

What does this evidence establish?

World Bank public remittance interfaces do not expose Yemen history uniformly. A surface reviewed on 2026-09-10 showed an older span while other World Bank surfaces and prior documented access vintages contained later observations. The difference is an interface/provenance state, not evidence that later underlying data are absent.

What does it measure?

The difference, as reviewed on 10 September 2026, between the span of Yemen remittance observations shown on one World Bank public data interface and the later observations on other World Bank surfaces and in earlier documented access.

Who or what does it apply to?

Source/interface-specific

When was it measured or observed?

World Bank public data surfaces as reviewed on 10 September 2026, and earlier documented access

How current is it?

The interfaces were reviewed on 10 September 2026, and what each shows may have changed since. The record should not be read as describing a later state of the interfaces unless they are reviewed again.

What this evidence does not establish

The difference does not show that data were deleted or withdrawn, or why any correction was made, and one public surface's observations are not a substitute for another's.

Limits of the measure

An interface endpoint does not establish underlying dataset absence, deletion or revision cause.
